evidence.quote: si igitur ultimam illam partem mittamus, ubi P 2 m. nullius plane auctoritatis est, efficitur stemma codicum hoc: Archetypus | P | ... | V M | F (diagram garbled)
quibus cum accedat, quod epistulae II 40 et 51 in V et F altera post III 42 altera post III 40 insertae sunt, iam de cognatione eorum dubitari nequit.
archetypum, ex quo classis deterior pendet, eius simillimum fuisse, ex quo P fluxit; nunc vero ... non solum similem, sed etiam eundem fuisse statuemus, postquam P ex eo descriptus est
Et inter se quidem Γ et Φ artiore vinculo cohaerere videntur, quam cum VMF

texts.notes: Two stemmata printed (p. XXXII partial, p. XXXVII complete), both garbled in OCR; reconstructed from the text: P vs. the 'classis deterior' (VMF + Γ Φ) copied from the same archetype after it was corrected. Π placed with P because the preface calls the Divionensis an apograph of the Parisinus (footnote 41, line ~1405) — verify on the page image whether the diagram hangs Π under P. Only P, V, M, F are extant direct witnesses.

evidence.quote: utrum codex eius ex diverso archetypo descriptus sit, quam ex quo T et M fluxerunt, an ex eodem.
nihilominus credo, Γ non meliorem quidem fontem esse, quam T et M, sed tamen ex communi horum archetypo non pendentem
tamen semper quoque ex fonte genuino ab archetypo codicum T et M diverso derivata esse potest.
commuuis utriusque editionis archetypus nullus alius est, quam autographum ipsum auctoris

texts.notes: Small 'Stemma codicum' printed above the text (line ~31482, garbled: 'T M'). Only two direct codices; the second branch is Gelenius' edition. For relatio III a separate higher split exists: Ambrosian recension (A) vs Symmachian edition (TMΓ), both from the autograph.
